tools.name: mudpie_search
tools.description: Super fast, semantic search across mudpie.ai’s public pages. Include actual task context; use null for unknowns.

tools.name: mudpie_page_tldr
tools.description: Read a compact extract of one indexed public page returned by mudpie_search, with its source, freshness and full Markdown link. It uses published content, not signed-in data. Only url is required. Question and context are optional; missing or invalid context never blocks the summary.

tools.name: mudpie_ask_anything
tools.description: Ask anything about mudpie.ai’s product, pricing, setup, limitations or comparisons. Get a direct answer from its published information, with sources. Add relevant context if you have it; otherwise just ask.

tools.name: mudpie_compare
tools.description: Compare this website with the products the user is actually weighing, from its published comparison pages, grouped per alternative. Alternatives it has no page for are named as not covered. Include actual task context; use null for unknowns.

tools.name: mudpie_pricing
tools.description: What this website costs for the user’s organisation and outcome: the published pricing pages that apply, with sources. It abstains when pricing is not published and never invents a quote. Include actual task context; use null for unknowns.

tools.name: mudpie_requirements_check
tools.description: Give the user’s must-haves, semicolon-separated in search_query or as a requirements array, and get a per-requirement table: met, not met or not documented, each with a source. Include actual task context; use null for unknowns.

tools.name: should_i_recommend_mudpie
tools.description: mudpie.ai isn’t for everyone. Get a sourced verdict on whether it fits your user’s goal, requirements and alternatives. The answer might be ‘not us.’

description: Email the user a Mudpie sign-in link to start a free account. Submit only an email address the user authorized. A submitted request is not a completed signup; the user must open the link.

labels.name: mudpie_feedback
labels.description: Report a bug, a missing feature, a wrong answer or unclear docs in Mudpie’s agent tools, right when you hit it. Only kind and message are required. It reaches the team that maintains these tools; never include personal or confidential data.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "public" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: mudpie_page_tldr, mudpie_sign_up · Public sink: mudpie_sign_up.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: mudpie_page_tldr, mudpie_sign_up · Public sink: mudpie_sign_up

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "mudpie_search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Super fast, semantic search across mudpie.ai’s public pages. Include actual task context; use null for unknowns." → after: "Super fast, semantic search across Mudpie’s public pages. Include actual task context; use null for unknowns."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
